detail.longDescription: Hi HN. Pokémon cards are one of my hobbies, and the question that comes up over and over is whether a raw card is worth paying PSA $40 or more to grade, or whether you should just sell it. The honest answer is usually "skip", but most pre-grading tools give you one confident grade and no math. Grade or Skip takes a photo of the front and back and does three things: - Measures centering with OpenCV. It finds the card, corrects perspective, measures each border and draws what it measured. If it can't trust a read, it says "not measured" instead of guessing. On 20 synthetic test sides the mean error is about 0.5 points of centering. That's synthetic, not real scans. - Asks a vision model (Claude or OpenAI with your key, or none) about corners, edges and surface. This is the weak part: in my testing it found 3 of 9 labelled defects. The README says so up front. - Turns that into a grade range (PSA 8–9, never one number) and the expected value of grading versus selling raw, using PSA's current tiers and fees, with every step shown. The screenshot in the README is a Psyduck at 53/47 with no visible defects and a likely 9–10, and grading it still loses about $26. Stack: FastAPI, Jinja, vanilla JS, SQLite and OpenCV, with no build step. AGPL-3.0. `docker compose up` and it runs on localhost. Without an AI key you still get centering and the money math. Where I'd love help: nobody has compared its estimates with real PSA results yet, so there's no accuracy number. If you photograph cards before sending them in, scripts/calibrate.py takes the front, the back and the grade that came back. If you don't collect, the quickest way to see it is gradeorskip.com/worth-grading, which runs the money math on this week's chase cards with no photo. Two come out opposite ways: an $84 Meowth ex leaves you about $59 behind if it grades a 9, while a $58 Pikachu ex pays with just a 9% chance of a 10. With a card in hand, the first scan at gradeorskip.com needs no sign-in, and after the free checks it's a one-time $5 for 25. I'm here all day for questions.
